chunks: From him, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from the one who narrated it, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:
When you love a man, do not joke with him and do not argue with him.

key_terms.أَحْبَبْتَ: You loved (past tense, addressing a male)
key_terms.تُمَارِهِ: You argue/dispute with him (from mumarah, implying contentious debate)
key_terms.تُمَازِحْهُ: You joke/tease him (from muzayah, implying playful banter)

ai.seo_question: What is the proper etiquette when interacting with someone you love according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this concise maxim from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), highlighting that while affection is the foundation of strong bonds, excessive levity (muzayah) can erode respect, and contentious debate (mumarah) can breed resentment. This teaching reflects the Shia emphasis on adab (etiquette) in social relations, where maintaining the dignity of the beloved is paramount to preserving spiritual and emotional harmony. It serves as a practical guideline for balancing warmth with seriousness in interpersonal dynamics.
